back: Moving all or part of a business from one location to another.
Raw materials, market, transport, labour, power and water, land, government policy, related firms, climate.
Nearness to customers and footfall, rent, competitors, convenience, security and access; online firms need internet.
Bulk-reducing (sugar milling, ore processing): near raw materials. Bulk-increasing (drinks, furniture): near the market.
Raw materials exhausted, market declines or moves, rising costs, natural disasters, government policy, need to expand.

front: Choosing a country to operate in?
back: Costs, markets and trading blocs, government and stability, skills and infrastructure, currency, laws and culture.
Moving equipment, lost production, staff payments or loss of skilled staff, lost customers.
Compare costs and expected revenue using the data, add qualitative factors, then justify a choice.
